mainTopic: Immersing vessels around יום טוב (בין השמשות, extra immersions), and which קרבנות may be brought on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: one answer says the משנה follows the רבנן and is entirely about שבת. Next comes a ברייתא. The תנא קמא forbids immersing an impure vessel during בין השמשות on ערב יום טוב. רבי שמעון שזורי forbids it even on a weekday, because the vessel needs הערב שמש. The רבנן of רב's בית מדרש explain the dispute as whether a person's rushing shows that he knows about הערב שמש. רבא disagrees and places the dispute in the case of someone who did not know that a שרץ smaller than a lentil does not make things impure. A ברייתא then explains מגב לגב and מחבורה לחבורה: an extra immersion that changes nothing is allowed on יום טוב. A new משנה brings the dispute of בית שמאי and בית הלל about bringing שלמים and עולות on יום טוב and doing סמיכה on them. עולא limits the dispute to the festival's required offerings and says everyone forbids נדרים ונדבות. The גמרא defends him against a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, either by correcting its wording or, as רב יוסף says, by treating it as a dispute among תנאים. The proof for this continues onto the next amud.

steps.title: Second answer: the משנה follows the רבנן and speaks only of שבת
steps.stepSummary: An alternative answer to the earlier problem. The משנה follows the רבנן, and the whole משנה is talking about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that the משנה follows the רבנן, and the entire משנה is talking about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the discussion from the previous section by giving a second way to explain the משנה. It says the משנה matches the רבנן, and every case in it is about שבת, not יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה's ban on immersing a vessel seemed to clash with the רבנן, who allow immersing vessels on יום טוב. This answer removes the clash by moving the whole משנה to שבת. On שבת, immersing a vessel is forbidden even according to the רבנן, so there is no longer any contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the tail end of the discussion on the previous עמוד, giving a second answer to a question already asked there.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: Introduces a second, alternative answer.

phrases.english: and the entire Mishnah is about Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Every case in the משנה refers to שבת, not יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier's discussion by offering a second resolution of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the case (the whole משנה is about שבת rather than יום טוב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ban on immersing seemed to refer to יום טוב, which would contradict the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the רבנן and deals entirely with שבת, where immersing a vessel is forbidden.

steps.title: ברייתא: an impure vessel may not be immersed at twilight before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a vessel which became impure on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed during בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a vessel that became impure on ערב יום טוב may not be immersed during בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It says you may not immerse an impure vessel during twilight on the eve of יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בין השמשות is a doubtful time: it may still be day, or it may already be יום טוב. Immersing vessels is forbidden on יום טוב, so the תנא קמא forbids it during this doubtful time as well. His reason is tied to the יום טוב, not to the vessel itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, a time of doubt whether it is day or night

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: A vessel that became impure on the eve of a Festival,
one may not immerse it during twilight.
phrases.notes: Twilight might already be יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure vessel may not be immersed during בין השמשות on ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון שזורי: even on a weekday, because the vessel needs sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי extends the ban to ordinary weekdays, because an immersed vessel needs הערב שמש before it is fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון שזורי says: even on a weekday we do not immerse it at twilight, because it needs הערב שמש.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא forbids immersing at twilight even when tomorrow is a regular weekday. His reason has nothing to do with יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After immersion, a vessel is not fully pure until the sun sets. If you immerse it during twilight, you cannot know whether that sunset still counts. רבי שמעון שזורי therefore avoids the doubtful situation altogether. His concern is the vessel's purification process, not the holiness of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
Sunset, needed to complete purification after immersion

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the puzzle in the next step. It sounds as if the תנא קמא does not care about הערב שמש, which is a basic rule of טהרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says:
even on a weekday one may not immerse it,
phrases.notes: That is, at twilight.

phrases.english: because it requires sunset.
phrases.notes: Full purity comes only after sunset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אַף בַּחוֹל אֵין מַטְבִּילִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disputing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersion at twilight is forbidden even on a weekday, because the vessel requires הערב שמש.

steps.title: Does the תנא קמא not require sunset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the implication that the תנא קמא does not require הערב שמש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does the תנא קמא not require הערב שמש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question. It seems the תנא קמא would allow twilight immersion on a weekday, as if he ignored the need for sunset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that an immersed vessel needs הערב שמש. So רבי שמעון שזורי's reason cannot be the real point of disagreement. The גמרא is pushing to find what the two opinions actually argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.confusionAlert: No one actually holds that sunset is unnecessary. The question shows that the dispute must lie somewhere else.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא בָּעֵי הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ?
phrases.english: And does the first tanna not require sunset?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical challenge: of course he requires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא בָּעֵי הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the implied position of the תנא קמא based on רבי שמעון שזורי's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the תנא קמא permits weekday twilight immersion despite the need for הערב שמש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הערב שמש is a universal requirement, so it cannot be what separates the two opinions.

steps.title: רבא reports the רבנן דבי רב: the dispute is about whether intention is evident from actions
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that the רבנן of the בית מדרש of רב explained that the dispute is about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I found the רבנן of the school of רב sitting and saying that they disagree about whether a person's intention is recognizable from his actions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports how the רבנן of רב's בית מדרש answered the question: both opinions agree that sunset is needed, and they argue about whether we can read a person's plan from how he acts. רבא himself will reject this explanation in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is no longer whether sunset is required. The question is whether this person's behavior shows that he knows the vessel needs הערב שמש. If it does, there is no worry that he will use the vessel too early, so immersing at twilight on a weekday is fine. The גמרא explains the exact case next.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the בית מדרש of רב
His intention is evident from his actions

steps.whyThisMatters: מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו is a recurring principle across ש״ס: when can behavior reveal a person's intent?

phrases.english: Rava said:
I found the Sages of the school of Rav
sitting and saying:
they disagree about whether his intention is evident from his actions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבָא: אַשְׁכַּחְתִּינְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different underlying principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute seemed to be about whether הערב שמש is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree that sunset is required. They argue about whether a person's intention can be read from his actions.

steps.title: What is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the concrete scenario of this dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a real-life example of the dispute before explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An abstract principle like 'intention is evident from actions' needs a concrete case to make sense. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete case behind רבא's principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific scenario where the two views about intention and actions differ

steps.title: The case: running at twilight to immerse a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The case is a person holding a vessel and running at בין השמשות to immerse it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a person is holding a vessel in his hand and running at בין השמשות to immerse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the scene: someone rushes at twilight to immerse his vessel. This is the act from which we might read his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view treats his rushing as proof that he knows the vessel needs הערב שמש, so he will not use it too early. The other view says the rushing proves nothing about what he knows. The גמרא will spell out how each side applies this.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone requires הערב שמש after immersion. According to the רבנן of רב's בית מדרש, the real dispute is whether a person's rushing at twilight shows that he knows the vessel needs הערב שמש.

phrases.english: for example, where he was holding a vessel in his hand,
and running along at twilight
to immerse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute concerns someone rushing at בין השמשות with a vessel in hand to immerse it.

steps.title: What each side reads into the running
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן think the running shows he knows he needs הערב שמש. רבי שמעון שזורי thinks he may just be rushing because of his work.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: the fact that he is running shows he knows the vessel needs sunset. The other master holds: he is running because of his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side reads the man who is running to the מקוה at בין השמשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say his hurry proves he knows the vessel is not pure until nightfall. So on a weekday there is no worry that he will use it too early. רבי שמעון שזורי says the hurry may only be about finishing his work, so it proves nothing about what he knows. That is why he forbids immersing at בין השמשות even on a weekday.
steps.confusionAlert: The first מר here is the רבנן (the lenient side), and the second מר is רבי שמעון שזורי. In step 10 the order is flipped.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: הַאי דְּקָא רָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל —
phrases.english: One master holds: this that he is running along —
phrases.notes: The רבנן / תנא קמא

phrases.english: he surely knows that it requires sunset.
phrases.notes: So there is no fear he will use it the same day

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מֵחֲמַת מְלַאכְתּוֹ הוּא דְּקָרָהֵיט.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: it is because of his work that he is running.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון שזורי

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: הַאי דְּקָא רָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each side reads the case given in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read the running as proof that he knows about הערב שמש. רבי שמעון שזורי reads it as hurrying for work.

steps.title: רבא moves the dispute to a different case
steps.stepSummary: רבא says everyone agrees to מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו. He places the dispute in a case where someone asked about a שרץ smaller than a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to them: about 'his intention is recognized from his actions,' everyone agrees. They argue in a case where a vessel touched less than a lentil-size of a שרץ, and the owner came to the Rabbis to ask: does it become impure from less than a lentil-size or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the explanation of the רבנן of רב's בית מדרש and offers a new case where the argument really lies. This step sets up the case, and the next step gives each side's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, both sides agree that a person's actions can show what he is thinking. So the running case cannot be the point of argument. Instead, the argument is about a man who showed he does not know a basic הלכה: a שרץ smaller than a lentil does not make things impure.

keyTerms.meaning: and I said to them (רבא speaking)
the size of a lentil, the minimum amount of a שרץ that makes things impure

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a principle can be accepted by everyone while the argument is only about how much we can assume a particular person knows.

phrases.english: And I said to them:
phrases.notes: רבא answering the רבנן of רב's בית מדרש

phrases.english: regarding 'his intention is recognized from his actions' —
everyone agrees, they do not argue.
phrases.notes: Everyone accepts the principle

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי כְּגוֹן דְּאִיטַּמִּי בְּפָחוֹת מִכַּעֲדָשָׁה,
phrases.english: Where they argue is, for example, where it became impure through less than a lentil-size,
phrases.notes: A שרץ smaller than a lentil does not really make things impure

phrases.english: and he came before the Rabbis to ask:
does it become impure through less than a lentil-size or not?
phrases.notes: His question shows he is not knowledgeable

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation from steps 5-8 and offers a different case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the dispute is about מחשבתו ניכרת מתוך מעשיו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone accepts that principle, so it cannot be what the two sides argue about

steps.title: Does ignorance of one law mean ignorance of הערב שמש?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון שזורי assumes that someone who did not know the lentil-size rule also does not know about הערב שמש. The רבנן say he still knows about הערב שמש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: since he did not learn this, he also did not learn about sunset. The other master holds: it is this he did not learn, but sunset he did learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives each side's reasoning in his new case. This completes his answer to the קשיא from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון שזורי says a person who did not know the lentil-size rule probably does not know about הערב שמש either, so he might use the vessel too early. The רבנן say the lentil rule is a detail, but הערב שמש is basic and well known, since it is written in the תורה. So the רבנן also need הערב שמש. They simply trust that this man knows it.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both sides require הערב שמש. They only argue about whether a person who does not know one law can be trusted to know about הערב שמש.

phrases.english: One master holds: since this he did not learn,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון שזורי

phrases.english: sunset he also did not learn,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: הָא הוּא דְּלָא גְּמִיר,
phrases.english: and the other master holds: it is this that he did not learn,
phrases.notes: The רבנן / תנא קמא

phrases.english: but sunset he did learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of each side in רבא's new case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving the dispute to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא seemed not to require הערב שמש
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides require הערב שמש. They argue only about whether an unlearned person knows it.

steps.title: What does 'from גב to גב' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase מטבילין מגב לגב and brings a ברייתא that asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And we immerse from גב to גב.' The Rabbis taught: how is 'from גב to גב' done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and starts a ברייתא that explains it. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words מגב לגב are unclear, so the ברייתא asks what kind of immersion they mean. This begins a new topic, separate from the הערב שמש discussion.

phrases.english: And we immerse from one 'gav' to another.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
phrases.notes: A ברייתא

phrases.english: How is 'from gav to gav'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the next phrase of the משנה

steps.title: Immersing the pitcher again for the winepress
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer: a person who wants to make his winepress-purity on top of the purity of his pitcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who wants to make his winepress on top of his pitcher...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts to answer: someone who already immersed his pitcher now wants to immerse it again, this time for use with his winepress. The ruling that this is allowed comes in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pitcher was already immersed once, for use as a pitcher. Now the owner changed his mind and wants to immerse it again for use with his winepress. מגב לגב means immersing again when you switch from one purpose to another. The second immersion does not change the vessel's status, as step 13 explains.

keyTerms.meaning: on top of, in addition to

phrases.english: One who wants to make his winepress
on top of his pitcher,
phrases.notes: The answer continues next

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת גִּתּוֹ עַל גַּב כַּדּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the ברייתא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Immersing a pitcher again so it can be used for the winepress (the answer continues)

steps.title: Finishing the answer: a second immersion of the pitcher is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes explaining מגב לגב: a person who already immersed his pitcher for his winepress may immerse it again on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and his pitcher on top of his winepress, he may do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the sentence it started in step 12. It rules that this extra immersion of the pitcher is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pitcher was already immersed once, for the winepress. Now he wants to immerse it again. The second טבילה does not change its status from טמא to טהור, so it does not count as a real טבילה. That is why it is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He may do it (it is allowed)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as permission to do any טבילה on יום טוב. It only covers an extra immersion of something already immersed, where nothing changes from טמא to טהור.

phrases.english: and his pitcher on top of his winepress
phrases.notes: The reverse case: he first immersed it for the winepress and now wants to immerse it again as a pitcher

phrases.english: he may do it.
phrases.notes: The ruling: allowed on יום טוב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the ברייתא's question that began in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does מטבילין מגב לגב mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An extra immersion done on top of an earlier one (pitcher on top of winepress-purity) is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: What does 'from group to group' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks how to understand the second phrase of the משנה, מחבורה לחבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is 'from group to group'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and asks what it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed two cases of allowed extra immersion. The ברייתא already explained the first, מגב לגב. Now it asks the same question about the second, מחבורה לחבורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A group signed up together to eat a קרבן פסח

phrases.english: How is 'from group to group'?
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה's phrase and asks for its meaning

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to step 11, now about the second phrase of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case does מחבורה לחבורה describe?

steps.title: Switching groups: a second immersion is allowed
steps.stepSummary: If someone planned to eat with one group and now wants to eat with another, he may immerse again on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was going to eat with this group, and now he wants to eat with a different group. He has permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. A person who already immersed to eat with one group may immerse again on יום טוב for a new group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was already טהור for the first group. The new immersion is only extra, so it does not change anything. Just like the pitcher, it is not a real טבילה, and it is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: He has permission; it is up to him

steps.whatToRemember: Both מגב לגב and מחבורה לחבורה follow one rule. A second immersion that is not needed is not a real טבילה, so it is allowed on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He was going to eat with this group,
phrases.notes: He already immersed for this group

phrases.english: and he wants to eat with a different group —
phrases.notes: Now he wants to immerse again for the new group

phrases.english: he has permission.
phrases.notes: Allowed even on יום טוב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and closes the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Switching from one פסח group to another allows an extra immersion on יום טוב.

steps.title: New משנה: bringing שלמים and עולות on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow שלמים without סמיכה and do not allow עולות. בית הלל allow both, and allow סמיכה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: We may bring peace-offerings but may not lean on them, and not burnt-offerings. בית הלל say: We may bring peace-offerings and burnt-offerings and lean on them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: which קרבנות may be brought on יום טוב, and whether one may do סמיכה on them. בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים are mostly eaten by people, so slaughtering them counts as preparing food. בית שמאי still ban סמיכה, because leaning on an animal counts as using it, which the רבנן forbade on יום טוב. They ban עולות, which are burned entirely and not eaten by anyone. בית הלל allow it all.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, mostly eaten by the owners
Burnt-offerings, burned entirely on the מזבח
Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is slaughtered
The two classic schools of תנאים

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the topic for the rest of the sugya. Two separate questions are involved: bringing the קרבן at all, and doing סמיכה on it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
phrases.notes: A new משנה begins

phrases.english: We may bring peace-offerings
phrases.notes: On יום טוב

phrases.english: but we do not lean on them,
phrases.notes: סמיכה counts as using an animal

phrases.english: but not burnt-offerings.
phrases.notes: Not eaten by people, so not food preparation

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
We may bring peace-offerings and burnt-offerings
and we lean on them.
phrases.notes: Even סמיכה is allowed

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה and a new topic, after the ברייתא was finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: שלמים yes but no סמיכה, and no עולות. בית הלל: שלמים and עולות, with סמיכה.

steps.title: עולא: the dispute is only about the holiday's required offerings
steps.stepSummary: עולא says the dispute is about סמיכה on שלמי חגיגה, and about bringing עולת ראייה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The dispute is about holiday peace-offerings, regarding leaning, and about the appearance burnt-offering, regarding bringing it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא narrows the משנה's dispute. It is only about the two offerings the holiday itself requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said שלמים and עולות in general. עולא says it means only the required holiday offerings. For שלמי חגיגה, the question is only about סמיכה. For עולת ראייה, the question is whether it may be brought at all. The implication is that private vows and free-will offerings are not part of this dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: The required peace-offering brought for the holiday
The required burnt-offering brought when appearing in the בית המקדש on the holiday
To be offered (brought on the מזבח)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ulla said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא begins

phrases.english: The dispute is about holiday peace-offerings, regarding leaning,
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees they may be brought; the argument is only about סמיכה

phrases.english: and about the appearance burnt-offering, regarding bringing it.
phrases.notes: The argument is whether it may be offered on יום טוב at all

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשַׁלְמֵי חֲגִיגָה לִסְמוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly which cases the משנה's dispute covers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is limited to סמיכה on שלמי חגיגה and to bringing עולת ראייה.

steps.title: The פסוק behind each side's view
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי read וחגתם as allowing only the חגיגה. בית הלל read לה׳ as allowing anything brought to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בית שמאי hold: 'You shall celebrate it as a holiday to ה׳.' The חגיגה, yes. The appearance burnt-offering, no. And בית הלל hold: 'To ה׳' means anything that is for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains, as part of עולא's words, where each side gets its view about עולת ראייה. Each side focuses on a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי focus on וחגתם, which sounds like חגיגה. So only the שלמי חגיגה is allowed on יום טוב, not the עולת ראייה. בית הלל focus on לה׳. Anything brought for ה׳, the עולה included, may be brought on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall celebrate it as a holiday to ה׳‎' (ויקרא כג:מא)

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, the argument over עולת ראייה comes from one פסוק. בית שמאי focus on וחגתם (only the חגיגה), and בית הלל focus on לה׳ (anything for ה׳).

phrases.english: For Beit Shammai hold:
'You shall celebrate it as a holiday to ה׳,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כג:מא

phrases.english: the holiday peace-offering, yes,
phrases.notes: וחגתם points to the חגיגה

phrases.english: the appearance burnt-offering, no.
And Beit Hillel hold:
'To ה׳': anything that is for ה׳.
phrases.notes: Includes the עולת ראייה

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי וְחַגֹּתֶם אוֹתוֹ חַג לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning from a פסוק for the dispute עולא just defined
steps.raayaObject: Whether עולת ראייה may be brought on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא כג:מא, וחגתם אותו חג לה׳: בית שמאי read וחגתם, בית הלל read לה׳

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no vow and gift offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: עולא adds that נדרים ונדבות are not brought on יום טוב according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not offered on יום טוב, according to all opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes his statement. He limits the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל to festival offerings only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, עולא said the dispute was only about סמיכה on שלמי חגיגה and about bringing עולת ראייה. Here he adds that offerings with no link to the festival, such as נדרים ונדבות, are forbidden by everyone, even בית הלל. בית הלל's reading of לה׳ in Step 18 only covers offerings that belong to the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: Vow-offerings: a person said 'I take upon myself to bring an offering'
Gift-offerings: a person said 'this animal is an offering'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית הלל allow every offering on יום טוב. In עולא's view, בית הלל only allow offerings that belong to the festival itself.

phrases.english: But vow-offerings and gift-offerings

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: all agree they are not offered on a Festival.
phrases.notes: Even בית הלל agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes עולא's statement by marking where the dispute stops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה says the same
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה independently rules that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אדא בר אהבה also said: vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second אמורא who agrees with עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וכן אמר show that another אמורא holds the same view. This makes עולא's rule look widely accepted, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise said; introduces an agreeing opinion
An אמורא who agrees with עולא here

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And likewise Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אֵין קְרֵיבִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: Vow-offerings and gift-offerings are not offered on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 19 with an agreeing אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the cases where there is no dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא with a ברייתא. Its first half lists the cases where בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about an עולה that is not for the festival, which is not offered on יום טוב. They also did not argue about שלמים that are for the festival, which are offered on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against עולא. This first half of the ברייתא prepares the ground; the real problem comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says everyone forbids a non-festival עולה. Notice that it only mentions an עולה here. It says nothing yet about non-festival שלמים, and that gap is where the contradiction will appear.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
A תנא who reports the dispute differently
Belonging to the festival, an offering required because of the חג

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיבִי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: They objected: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: about a burnt-offering that is not of the Festival,
that it is not offered on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are of the Festival,
that they are offered on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיבִי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the rule in Steps 19 and 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that everyone forbids non-festival offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This half only sets up the challenge. The actual contradiction comes in the next half of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא says they disagree about non-festival peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the dispute is about a festival עולה and about non-festival שלמים, with בית הלל allowing both. This contradicts עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? An עולה that is for the festival, and שלמים that are not for the festival. בית שמאי say he may not bring them, and בית הלל say he may.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the core of the challenge. The ברייתא says בית הלל allow non-festival שלמים on יום טוב, but עולא said everyone forbids them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-festival שלמים are נדרים ונדבות. According to this ברייתא, בית הלל permit them, which directly contradicts עולא and רב אדא בר אהבה's claim of דברי הכל.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: About a burnt-offering that is of the Festival,
phrases.notes: For example, the עולת ראייה.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are not of the Festival.
phrases.notes: These are נדרים ונדבות, the source of the contradiction.

phrases.english: For Beit Shammai say: He may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say: He may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and brings out the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that everyone forbids נדרים ונדבות on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says בית הלל allow non-festival שלמים, which are נדרים ונדבות. So the matter is disputed, not agreed by all.

steps.title: Correcting the ברייתא's wording to match עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא: everyone forbids both non-festival עולות and non-festival שלמים. The only dispute is about the festival עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fix the text and read it this way: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about an עולה or שלמים that are not for the festival, which are not offered on יום טוב. They also did not argue about שלמים that are for the festival, which are offered. They argued only about an עולה that is for the festival: בית שמאי say he may not bring it, and בית הלל say he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the ברייתא so it agrees with עולא. Non-festival שלמים move from the 'disputed' list to the 'everyone forbids' list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two changes are made. First, 'non-festival שלמים' is added to the cases everyone forbids. Second, it is removed from the dispute. That leaves only the festival עולה, such as the עולת ראייה, under dispute, exactly as עולא said in Step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Fix the text and say it like this; introduces a correction of the wording
Burnt-offering, completely burned on the מזבח
Peace-offerings, mostly eaten by the owners

steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, as supported by the corrected ברייתא: festival שלמים may be brought according to everyone (עולא places the dispute only over their סמיכה); non-festival offerings (נדרים ונדבות) are forbidden by everyone; and bringing the festival עולה is disputed, with בית הלל allowing it.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not making up a new opinion. It is fixing the wording of the ברייתא so that it fits a view already held by two אמוראים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: when an אמורא's view is strongly held, the גמרא may adjust the wording of a ברייתא instead of rejecting the אמורא.

phrases.english: Fix it and say as follows:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: about burnt-offerings and peace-offerings that are not of the Festival,
phrases.notes: Here is the correction: שלמים are added to the 'everyone forbids' list.

phrases.english: that they are not offered on a Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁלָמִים שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and about peace-offerings that are of the Festival,
that they are offered on a Festival.
About what did they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: עַל עוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: About a burnt-offering that is of the Festival,
phrases.notes: Non-festival שלמים no longer appear here.

phrases.english: For Beit Shammai say: He may not bring it,
and Beit Hillel say: He may bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Steps 21 and 22 by correcting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as first quoted says בית הלל allow non-festival שלמים on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The corrected ברייתא says everyone forbids all non-festival offerings, and the only dispute is the festival עולה, matching עולא.

steps.title: רב יוסף says there is no need to correct the ברייתא because תנאים disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the need to change the ברייתא. He says the issue is a dispute among תנאים, so עולא can follow another opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Have you removed all the תנאים from the world?! This is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second, different way to save עולא from the challenge. He says the ברייתא can stay exactly as it is, because other תנאים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 23, the גמרא changed the words of the ברייתא so it would match עולא. רב יוסף says that is unnecessary. The ברייתא reflects one תנא's view, and עולא's "everyone agrees" can be understood as following a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era. Here it means "a dispute among תנאים."

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not agreeing with the correction in Step 23. He offers a replacement for it: leave the ברייתא alone and treat it as one side of a dispute among תנאים.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Have you removed the Tannaim from the world?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. It means: why rewrite the text, when you could simply say other Tannaim disagree?

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the correction made in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic dispute (תנאי היא) instead of textual emendation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא had to be corrected, or else עולא would be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא stays as it is. It is one opinion among תנאים, and עולא follows another view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא strategy. Instead of rewriting a ברייתא to fit an אמורא, the גמרא can say the אמורא follows a different תנא.

steps.title: A ברייתא about leaning on festival peace-offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins quoting a ברייתא as proof that תנאים argue. בית שמאי say סמיכה on festival שלמים is done on ערב יום טוב. בית הלל say it is done on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: About שלמים brought because of the festival, on the festival, בית שמאי say: one leans on them on ערב יום טוב and slaughters them on יום טוב. בית הלל say: one leans on them on יום טוב and slaughters them on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts bringing a source to back up his claim that תנאים disagree. This ברייתא lays the groundwork, and the rest of the proof continues after this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is festival שלמים, such as שלמי חגיגה or שלמי שמחה. בית שמאי do not allow סמיכה on יום טוב, so they move it to the day before. בית הלל allow both the סמיכה and the שחיטה on יום טוב. This ברייתא shows בית שמאי and בית הלל arguing over festival שלמים, just as עולא said. But רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said there was no dispute about festival שלמים, so the תנאים disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: "As it is taught in a ברייתא": introduces a תנאי source
Peace-offerings brought because of the festival, such as חגיגה or שמחה
Does סמיכה: leans his hands on the animal before it is slaughtered

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that בית שמאי still allow the שחיטה itself on יום טוב. They only move the סמיכה to the day before.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלָמִים הַבָּאִים מֵחֲמַת יוֹם טוֹב בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: Peace-offerings that come because of the festival, on the festival,
Beit Shammai say:
One leans on them on the eve of the festival,
and slaughters them on the festival.
And Beit Hillel say:
One leans on them on the festival,
and slaughters them on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that is meant to show the dispute among תנאים that רב יוסף mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the issue is a dispute among תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on סמיכה for festival שלמים, where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree
